pages.title: Arrival (film)
pages.extract:
Arrival is a 2016 American science fiction drama film directed by Denis Villeneuve and adapted by Eric Heisserer.

== Plot ==
=== First Contact ===
Linguistics professor Louise Banks (Amy Adams) experiences visions of her daughter Hannah, who died at age twelve from an incurable illness[1]. Twelve extraterrestrial spacecraft, dubbed "shells", appear across Earth[citation needed]. US Army Colonel GT Weber (Forest Whitaker) recruits Louise and physicist Ian Donnelly (Jeremy Renner) to decipher the seven-limbed aliens' language at the Montana shell.

=== Decoding the Language ===
Inside the craft, Louise and Ian establish contact with two cephalopod-like heptapods, whom they name Abbott and Costello (played by CGI performers). Louise discovers that their written language consists of complex circular logograms lacking linear time. As she becomes fluent in the language, she realizes her visions of Hannah are not memories of the past, but flash-forwards of a future yet to happen, giving her the power to prevent a global military standoff while embracing the entirety of her daughter's life.

== Cast ==
* Amy Adams as Louise Banks
* Jeremy Renner as Ian Donnelly

== Production ==
Filming began in Montreal in June 2015.
